lines.text: There it is, {winner} takes the Showdown. Even our panel can agree on something at last.
After all the debating, {winnerClub} gets the final word. That's rather inconvenient for the rest of us.
Well, {loser} made this a rivalry worth watching, but the final honours belong to {winner}.
You can stop asking who takes it now. {winner} has answered that question rather comprehensively.
I'd ask for a recount of our forecasts, but the final standings have already made fools of the paperwork.
lines.was: The studio has run out of predictions, which is just as well. {winnerClub} has delivered the result.

lines.text: Give {winner} the title, and give {loser} some credit for making the contest matter.
Funny how all those competing opinions shrink once the champion is no longer a matter of opinion.
lines.was: Funny how a long-running argument becomes so simple once somebody actually wins the Showdown.

lines.text: That debate's officially finished. I shall miss sounding certain while being so regularly unsure.
With {winner} confirmed as champion, I suspect our prediction sheets would benefit from a discreet shredder.
Credit where it's due, {winnerClub} has seen the whole thing through and come away with the crown.
Goodbye to the ifs, the maybes and the hopeful little asterisks. We've arrived at the answer.
lines.was: All the possibilities are gone now, replaced by a lovely straightforward answer: {winner}.

lines.text: Quite a conclusion for {winner}. Every retelling of this Showdown now has a proper name to begin with.
lines.was: Quite a conclusion for {winner}. You build a rivalry over seasons, then sign your name underneath it.

lines.text: Turns out the most convincing pundit wasn't sitting here at all. It was the finished standings.
Stop me if I'm overthinking this, but the decisive detail appears to be {winner} winning the Showdown.
lines.was: Somebody put the debate away. The Showdown belongs to {winner}, and that's a proper conclusion.

lines.text: Here's the part nobody can argue with. {winner} has won the whole contest, not merely a chapter.
Put this rivalry in the archive with {winnerClub} on the title page. That's how it reads now.
lines.was: Now the season-by-season arguments can become stories, and {winnerClub} gets to write the ending.

lines.text: For {loserClub}, a worthy rivalry to look back on. For {winnerClub}, a title to treasure.
If {winner} needs an introduction now, just use the word champion. Saves everyone a lot of time.
Remarkable, isn't it? Every hypothetical disappears when the final result arrives, except the ones we'll keep debating.
Nobody's waiting on a hypothetical anymore. The Showdown has a champion, and there's nothing tentative about that.
lines.was: Nothing provisional about this. {winner} has secured the Showdown, and the conversation changes immediately.

lines.text: Imagine spending all that time preparing a closing argument, only for {winner} to produce the verdict.
Our congratulations go to {winner}. Our sympathies go to whoever backed the other prediction in this studio.
You can debate the route all evening, but {winnerClub} owns the destination. That's the awkward bit for us.
lines.was: An excellent reminder from {winnerClub} that forecasts are entertainment, but finishing top is the business.

lines.text: At the end, {winner} has what every manager wanted: the right to say the Showdown is theirs.
Let's have the applause for {winner}, and let's not forget {loser} helped make it worth winning.
I'd happily reopen the discussion, but the prize has already been claimed. A minor obstacle for television.
lines.was: I'd like to reopen the discussion, but the champion has rather spoiled that particular programme.

lines.text: You know what's refreshing? No conditional language left. {winner} has won, full stop.
That final tally speaks plainly, even if this panel has never shown the same talent.
Anyone still arguing with a completed table can borrow the studio's eraser. I doubt it'll help.
lines.was: So much for our finely balanced theories. {winnerClub} has put the conclusion beyond debate.

lines.text: Call it the end of the argument and the beginning of {winner}'s favourite story.
There's a difference between enjoying a season and owning the Showdown. We're looking at it now.
lines.was: Every little disagreement led here, and {winner} gets to own the answer at the end.

lines.text: Look at {winner} now, with the contest behind them and the champion's title beside their name.
lines.was: There's the finish, and there's {winner} standing above the rest of this particular rivalry.

lines.text: Before somebody asks for expert analysis, perhaps the experts should examine their own prediction records.
lines.was: For once, the panel doesn't need a second opinion. The Showdown champion is {winner}.

lines.text: I hope {winnerClub} enjoys this. Winning the entire contest deserves more than a polite nod.
Nobody should confuse losing a Showdown with having nothing to show for a fine rivalry.
We came here to pick a winner. {winner} was good enough to do that job for us.
My colleague's about to offer nuance. Before that, congratulations to {winner}, who actually won the thing.
lines.was: Not sure what my colleague's about to dispute. The competition is over and {winner} has won.

lines.text: Champions get the headlines, rivals give those headlines meaning. There's room for applause on both sides.
lines.was: A fine final answer from {winnerClub}, with enough shared history to make it really mean something.

lines.text: My advice to {winner}: frame the standings. My advice to us: stop trying to improve on them.
lines.was: You could frame the final standings. I'd advise {winner} to check the spelling on the plaque.

lines.text: That is a proper finish. {winner} can enjoy the victory without a footnote about what comes next.
What a relief for our long-suffering editor. The headline can simply read: {winner} wins the Showdown.
Here's a service announcement: champion is no longer a prediction. It's a title that's been claimed.
lines.was: By the time you say champion, everybody knows you're talking about {winner}. That's the difference today.

lines.text: Try finding a footnote on that final result. It fits perfectly well on the main line.
lines.was: The great thing for {winnerClub} is that this victory doesn't need any further qualification.

lines.text: From now on, {winner} can leave the second-guessing to us and concentrate on enjoying the title.
lines.was: I've watched this argument turn corners, but {winner} has finally brought it home.

lines.text: Spare a thought for {loser}. There is honour in helping make a triumph feel earned.
Grammar lesson from the studio: 'might win' has become 'has won.' Even I can manage that.
lines.was: Put the forecast cards aside, because {winner} has replaced possibility with something much better: certainty.

lines.text: And that, ladies and gentlemen, is what a completed rivalry looks like. A winner, and a story.
This has all the makings of a classic studio discussion, except the answer isn't up for grabs.
Perhaps the nicest compliment to {winner} is that the whole rivalry feels worthy of its champion.
We're going to need a new question for next time. This Showdown has already answered its own.
Plenty of room for shared memories, but the top line of the record belongs to the champion.
lines.was: The result belongs to {winner}; the memories belong to the rivalry. That's a fair division.

lines.text: Fine print won't change the headline. This Showdown has a champion, and the ink can finally dry.
lines.was: No complicated summary required for {winnerClub}. A Showdown started, and this club finished as champion.

lines.text: I wouldn't fancy arguing against the final standings, especially not with {winner} at the top.
Take all those competing theories, fold them neatly, and place them beneath the final standings.
lines.was: The final chapter has a name on it, and that name is {winner}. Lovely bit of closure.

lines.text: Before we crown {winner}, let's acknowledge the competition. Without {loser}, there's no rivalry to celebrate.
A completed Showdown is a funny thing. All that suspense, then a result you can say in a breath.
On the big question, this panel finally has a unanimous answer. We should probably mark the occasion.
No additional season is hiding in the small print. The champion has already crossed the finish.
lines.was: There's no appeal to future seasons. {winner} has taken the whole prize, right here.

lines.text: For the record, I always respected {winnerClub}. I merely had other opinions several times.
Whoever kept our prediction board deserves a break. {winner} has settled the debate for good.
One thing is certain, {loserClub} gave this contest its opposition, and {winnerClub} claimed the title.
Curious thing about endings: the argument has closed, but the bragging rights come with no expiry date.
lines.was: The competition can close its doors now, but {winner}'s achievement will be very easy to reopen.

lines.text: Look, everybody can have a theory. Only {winner} can have this Showdown title.
And with that, the trophy conversation changes from might to did. That's a lovely little shift.
I'll be gracious and congratulate {winner}, despite the considerable damage to my earlier predictions.
Suspense had a fine run. It must now give way to a rather more durable souvenir: victory.
lines.was: The suspense has packed its bags. It's leaving {winner} with the honour of champion.

lines.text: That's the result, then. A proper winner, a proper rivalry, and nobody here short of opinions.
A studio can speculate forever. Thankfully, the competition eventually insists on a definite answer.
lines.was: When it comes to finishing the job, {winnerClub} has left nothing for the studio to settle.

lines.text: Don't mistake the end of the contest for the end of the conversation. We'll be talking about this.
At least {winner} won't need the panel to vote on it. The Showdown has been won outright.
Tell the archive desk to file this under champion. {winner} has earned the heading.
We're all in agreement about the outcome. Frankly, that may be the night's bigger surprise.
Yesterday's grand theories are today's packing paper. The actual title won't need much wrapping.
lines.was: The question was who could win the Showdown. {winner} has made that a matter of history.

lines.text: Even those of us reluctant to concede a point can enjoy hearing the words 'Showdown champion' aloud.
lines.was: Trust me, {winnerClub} won't mind hearing this repeated. Showdown champions has a pleasing ring.

lines.text: If you're {loser}, you can take pride in the battle. The finished contest has a worthy champion.
What started as a rivalry has ended with {winner} holding the title. There's your full story.
I had a whole closing speech ready, but {winner} has rather stolen the best line.
Listen, the standings don't care which pundit sounded persuasive. They recognise {winner} as champion.
When the studio lights go out, the result stays. That is the real luxury of winning.
lines.was: The Showdown's finished, and that means {winner} has something the rest of us can only analyse.

lines.text: Against all our speculation, the simplest statement survives. {winner} is the overall winner.
It's amazing how quickly the room gets quiet when the final verdict doesn't need our help.
That is the kind of answer {winnerClub} can carry into every friendly argument that follows.
For anyone joining us late, {winner} has won the Showdown. Yes, the entire thing.
Maybe my colleague can explain the result differently. They cannot make it belong to anybody else.
Our closing analysis can wait. {winner} has supplied a much better final line by taking the Showdown.
lines.was: The final whistle is metaphorical here, but {winner}'s title is as real as the result.

lines.text: No need to dress it up, and no reason to play it down. {winner} is the champion.
Spare the superlatives for a moment. {winnerClub} has earned the best straightforward noun in the business: champion.
lines.was: You have to admire the finish from {winnerClub}. They leave the studio with a completed achievement.

lines.text: Somewhere in these papers is a prediction I got right. Fortunately, {winner} doesn't need to search.
Rivalry survives the closing credits, and a win like this gives it the sort of ending people keep quoting.
lines.was: The title is settled, the rivalry remains, and I reckon that makes for an excellent ending.

lines.text: Here comes my least favourite part of this job: admitting the result speaks better than I do.
Consider the curtain down on this Showdown. {winner} gets the bow, the rivalry gets the applause.
No other season can change this result now. {winner}'s place at the finish is secure.
And if {loser} wants a rematch someday, they'll have a champion worth taking on again.
Today's studio question has become tomorrow's trivia answer. It's {winner}, in case you wondered.
Every good argument deserves a conclusion. This one comes with a champion and a very long afterlife.
lines.was: We've spent seasons asking what might happen. {winnerClub} has given us something to remember instead.

lines.text: There goes the last uncertainty. The Showdown title is {winner}'s to enjoy.
I won't pretend the outcome was obvious, but I will say {winner} has made it official.
History won't record our best guesses, thankfully. It'll record {winner} as the Showdown champion.
There's an empty seat at the pundits' table for somebody who predicted this correctly. Very empty, apparently.
lines.was: The chair marked champion has an occupant now, and {winner} has every right to sit down.

lines.text: And that's the beauty of a rivalry with an ending. The argument stops, the respect doesn't.
